conf.description: arkime sessions summary-copy pull, deliberately narrow scope per recommendations.direct.cribl: renames only the two fields the recommendation leaves for Cribl (node, dns.host), gives http.uri a non-url.original custom home per its own field row's warning, and defers @timestamp/event.start/event.end synthesis, network.transport/iana_number derivation, and the http.uri host+path split to the separate Elastic ingest pipeline the recommendation explicitly assigns that work to.

conf.comment: arkime/sessions/api-pull. recommendations.direct.cribl scopes Cribl to a narrow summary-copy pull (firstPacket/lastPacket/source.ip/port/destination.ip/port/ipProtocol/network.bytes/node/http.uri/dns.host plus community_id) and assigns the ECS repair work (timestamp synthesis, network.transport/iana_number derivation, http.uri host+path split) to a SEPARATE Elastic ingest pipeline -- honored here per the brief's rule 4 rather than duplicating that work in Cribl. This pipeline only renames the two fields the recommendation leaves for Cribl (node, dns.host) and gives http.uri a non-url.original custom home per its own field row's explicit warning against trusting it as url.original. Gaps, not invented: no concrete length is given anywhere for the 'cap the free-text arrays' instruction; network.community_id's literal API field name is never tabled in this work order. Field selection/auth/backpressure/reconciliation are Source-level concerns, out of a pipeline's scope.

functions.description: document the deliberately narrow scope, the Cribl/Elastic division of labor, and the two unimplemented gaps

source.ip/port, destination.ip/port, network.bytes, firstPacket, lastPacket and ipProtocol are left untouched -- either already correctly ECS-named/nested by Arkime's own sessions3 schema, or explicitly reserved for the Elastic-side ingest pipeline per recommendations.direct.cribl
dataset-level constants only (no hyphen in event.dataset), independent of the Cribl/Elastic division of labor above
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
